text.p: * The first round of U.S.-Russian talks in Helsinki between Presidents Bill Clinton and Boris Yeltsin focused on security issues without a concrete outcome so far. Yeltsin reiterated Russia's opposition to NATO's eastward expansion.
A second round will follow with talks concentrating mainly on bilateral cooperation and economic ties.
* President Emil Constantinescu met ruling coalition leaders after talks with opposition leaders on Thursday.
Democratic Party and National Peasant Party leaders said a recent move by the opposition Party of Social Democracy to walk out of parliament sessions had not sparked a crisis.
They said they agreed with some of the opposition's claims regarding limits on the government's rule by decree and the need to appoint new administration boards for state radio and television.
* Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis met his Romanian counterpart Victor Ciorbea to discuss bilateral cooperation and to exchange opinions on the situation in the region.
Simitis said Greece supports Romania's bid to win quick admission to NATO and pleads for non-discriminating criteria for Eastern and Central European countries candidates to NATO membership.

* Romania and Greece share the same position on the issue of Turkish-Greek relations, Simitis told a news conference after talks with Ciorbea. The two countries believe tensions between Turkey and Greece should be solved in line with international laws and by resorting to the international court in The Hague, he said.
* Romania and Greece set up an inter-ministry commission.
* More than 90 percent of Romanians want their country to join the European Union, EU Integration Minister Alexandru Herlea told the Crans-Montana economic forum held in Bucharest.

* Greater Romania Party senator Vadim Tudor accused the government of pushing Romanians to the brink of starvation and of failing to fulfil electoral promises since appointement last December. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
